privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.body:
OpenCaves is a free, community-built map of the cenotes and caves of the Yucatán Peninsula. This policy explains what personal information OpenCaves collects, why, who it is shared with, and the choices and rights you have.

## Who is responsible

OpenCaves is operated by Christian Rémillard, in Québec, Canada, who is also the person in charge of the protection of personal information under Québec law. For any question or request about your personal information, write to [privacy@opencaves.org](mailto:privacy@opencaves.org).

## What we collect

**When you just browse.** You don't need an account to use the map. To make some features work, the app signs you in with an *anonymous session*: a random identifier with no name or email attached.

**When you create an account.** We store your email address and the name you choose. If you sign in with Google or Microsoft, we also receive the name and photo of that profile. Passwords are handled by our authentication provider (Firebase Authentication); we never see them.

**What you save or rate.** Cenotes you save are stored in your account and are private to you. When you rate a cenote, your rating is stored with your account identifier (not your name or email) and is used to compute the cenote's public average.

**What you contribute.** Photos, maps, videos and cave information you add are public: they are shown to everyone using OpenCaves. Uploaded files are linked to your account identifier and keep their original file name. The original photo is kept as uploaded, including any embedded data such as the location where it was taken (EXIF), and photos can show faces: please only share what you're comfortable making public.

**Your location.** When you use "Find my location" or "My location", your device's position is used on your device only, to center the map or fill in a coordinate. We don't store it or send it to our servers. It only becomes part of a cave's data if you save it in a coordinate field yourself.

**Technical information.** Like any website, the services that deliver OpenCaves (see below) receive technical information such as your IP address, browser type and the map area you view. We don't use advertising, and we don't use analytics or tracking cookies.

## How we use it

We use your information only to run OpenCaves: to sign you in, keep your saved cenotes and ratings, show and attribute contributions, protect the service against abuse, and answer your requests. We don't sell your personal information, and we don't use it for advertising or profiling.

## Who we share it with

OpenCaves relies on these service providers, who process information on our behalf or when you use their features:

- **Google Firebase and Google Cloud** (hosting, accounts, database, file storage, server functions).
- **Google and Microsoft**, only if you choose to sign in with them: they confirm who you are to OpenCaves.
- **Mapbox** (map images). Mapbox receives your IP address and the map area you view.
- **Google Maps Platform** (turning a cave's coordinates into a street address).
- **YouTube and Vimeo**, only when a video is embedded on a cenote and you play it. YouTube videos use its privacy-enhanced mode.

Some of these providers store or process information outside Québec and Canada, notably in the United States, where it is subject to local law. We use providers that offer protections consistent with Québec and Canadian privacy law.

## Information stored on your device

To work quickly and offline, OpenCaves stores data in your browser: your preferences, a copy of the cave data, and pictures and maps it downloads for offline use. This data stays on your device. You can clear the downloaded pictures and maps from your account page ("Offline use"), or all of it through your browser's settings.

## How long we keep it

We keep your account information for as long as you have an account. When your account is deleted, your saved cenotes and ratings are deleted with it. Contributions you made public (photos, maps, cave information) stay part of the open cave data unless you ask us to remove them. Technical logs kept by our providers are deleted on their own schedules.

## Your rights

You can ask to access the personal information we hold about you, correct it, or delete it. You can also withdraw your consent, ask us to stop using it, or receive a copy in a common format. You can change your name on your account page. For anything else, write to [privacy@opencaves.org](mailto:privacy@opencaves.org). We'll answer within 30 days. If you're not satisfied with our answer, you can complain to the *Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec*.

## Children

OpenCaves is not intended for children. Accounts are for people 14 and older. Younger children need a parent's or guardian's consent to create an account.

## Security

We use the security measures built into our providers (encrypted connections, access rules that let each person write only their own data, restricted administrator access). No online service is perfectly secure, so we'll tell you, and the Commission when required, of any incident that could seriously harm you.

## Changes

If we change this policy, we'll update the date above. For important changes, we'll let account holders know in advance.

## Contact

[privacy@opencaves.org](mailto:privacy@opencaves.org)

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.body:
These terms govern your use of OpenCaves, a free, community-built map of the cenotes and caves of the Yucatán Peninsula, operated by Christian Rémillard in Québec, Canada. By using OpenCaves, you agree to these terms.

## Safety first

**Cave and cenote diving can be dangerous and can kill.** OpenCaves is an information resource, not a guide, and it's no substitute for proper training, certification, equipment, local knowledge and good judgment.

The information on OpenCaves comes largely from the community. It can be incomplete, inaccurate or out of date. Conditions, access, fees, ownership and hazards change. Always check with the landowner, local operators and guides before you go, and dive within your training and limits.

## Access to caves

Many cenotes are on private or communal (*ejido*) land. Their presence on OpenCaves doesn't mean you may visit them. Respect the owners, their rules and their fees, and leave no trace.

## Your account

You're responsible for your account and for keeping your sign-in details private. Give accurate information, and don't use someone else's account. Accounts are for people 14 and older. Younger children need a parent's or guardian's consent.

## Contributing

You can add photos, maps, videos and cave information. By contributing, you confirm that:

- the content is yours, or you have the right to share it;
- it doesn't break anyone's rights (copyright, privacy, image) or the law;
- it doesn't include other people's personal information without their consent.

You keep the rights to your contributions, and you license them to everyone under the **Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0** license (CC BY-SA 4.0). Anyone may share and adapt them, with credit, under the same license. We may edit, move or remove any contribution, for example if it's inaccurate, off-topic or unsafe.

## Acceptable use

Don't use OpenCaves to harm others, post illegal, misleading or offensive content, collect other users' information, disrupt the service, or access it by automated means that put an unreasonable load on it.

## The cave data

The cave information on OpenCaves is open data, available under **CC BY-SA 4.0**. Credit "OpenCaves and contributors". Map images are provided by Mapbox and © OpenStreetMap contributors, under their own terms.

## Third-party services

OpenCaves links to and embeds services run by others, such as Google Maps directions, YouTube and Vimeo. Their own terms apply to them, and we're not responsible for them.

## No warranty

OpenCaves is provided free, "as is" and "as available", without any warranty of accuracy, completeness or availability. To the extent permitted by applicable law, including Québec's consumer protection law, we're not liable for any damage, injury or loss arising from your use of OpenCaves or of the information it contains.

## Changes and termination

We may change OpenCaves or these terms. If we make important changes, we'll update the date above and tell account holders in advance. We may suspend or close accounts that break these terms. You can stop using OpenCaves and ask us to delete your account at any time.

## Governing law

These terms are governed by the laws of Québec and of Canada applicable there. Disputes go to the courts of Québec, unless the law gives you the right to another forum.

## Contact

[privacy@opencaves.org](mailto:privacy@opencaves.org)

betaTesting.title: What can I do?
betaTesting.lead: OpenCaves is in beta, and you're one of its first divers. Use it the way you'd use it before and after a dive, and tell us what breaks, what confuses you, and what's missing.

report.title: Tell us
report.sub: Every report reaches the OpenCaves team by email. You need an account to send one.

bug.title: Something broke
bug.text: A page that won't load, a button that does nothing, a change that wasn't saved, a photo or a map that won't open.

misleading.title: Something is misleading
misleading.text: A label you don't understand, a feature that doesn't do what it says, or data that looks wrong: a position, an access, a depth.

idea.title: Something is missing
idea.text: A feature that would help you plan a dive or share one, or something you expected to find and didn't.

try.title: Try everything
try.sub: Nothing you do in the beta can break anything for good, so poke around.

explore.title: Explore
explore.text: The map, the cave and system lists, the search, a cave page and its sections.

edit.title: Edit caves
edit.text: Add a cave, its coordinates, its access, its texts; correct what looks wrong.

media.title: Add photos, videos, maps
media.text: From a cave's page: upload photos, link a video, add a survey map.

systems.title: Edit cave systems
systems.text: Their length and depth, their exploration history, how they connect.

offline.title: Go offline
offline.text: Install the app, save some caves, then use it with no signal, as in the jungle.

everywhere.title: Phone and computer
everywhere.text: Try it on your phone and on a computer, in light and dark mode.

languages.title: Every language
languages.text: English, French and Spanish: tell us about a translation that sounds wrong.

tips.title: How to report well
tips.one: One report per problem or idea.
tips.steps: Say what you did, what you expected, and what happened instead.
tips.page: The page you were on is filled in for you; change it if the problem is elsewhere.
tips.device: Your browser is added for you: say which device it is if it matters (for example, an Android phone).

reset.title: Beta data can be reset
reset.text: What you change now isn't permanent yet: the data can be replaced at any time before 1.0.

public.title: Everything you add is public
public.text: Don't share anyone's phone number, or anything you wouldn't want made public.

safety.title: OpenCaves is not for dive planning
safety.text: Cave diving can kill. Get trained, dive within your limits, and always check conditions on site.

feedback.title: Send feedback
feedback.intro: Tell the OpenCaves team about a bug, something misleading, or an idea. Thank you for helping!

kindText.misleading: Something is confusing or looks wrong.
kindText.idea: Something is missing or could be better.

hints.bug: Write the steps to reproduce it, one per line, so we can see it happen too: what you did, what you expected, and what happened instead.
hints.misleading: Say what is misleading - a label, a feature, some data - and what you understood. If data looks wrong, tell us what you think is right and how you know.
hints.idea: Describe what you would like OpenCaves to do, and when it would help you: before a dive, after one, to share something?

home.title: Open data for cave diving
home.description: OpenCaves: caves and cave systems for cave divers around the world - locations, access, survey maps, connections and exploration history, open and built by divers. Starting with the cenotes of the Yucatán.

hero.title: Open data for cave diving
hero.lead: OpenCaves gathers what cave divers want to know about caves and cave systems around the world: where they are, how to get in, how they connect, what the surveys show. Open, and built by divers. It starts with the cenotes of the Yucatán.
hero.searchPlaceholder: Find a cave, a system or an area

safety.title: Cave diving can kill
safety.text: Diving beyond the daylight zone of a cave or cenote takes cave training and certification, the right equipment and experience. Trained, experienced divers have died in caves. Never go beyond your training and limits, and never enter a cave you don't know without a qualified local guide.
safety.cavern: In a cenote, the cavern - the part where daylight still shows the way out - can be dived with cavern training and a guide; beyond it is the cave, for trained cave divers only.

disclaimer.title: Not for dive planning
disclaimer.text: The information on OpenCaves is shared by its community. It can be incomplete, inaccurate or out of date, and it is not suitable for planning or conducting a dive. You use it at your own risk: always check with local guides, dive centres and landowners before you go. See the

contribute.title: Built by divers
contribute.text: OpenCaves is open data: anyone can read it, and divers keep it up to date. Sign up to add caves, photos, videos and ratings, and get updates on new caves and systems. The app itself is open source.

welcome.title: Welcome to {{name}}!
welcome.intro: Grab your mask: {{name}} is a map of the underwater caves of the Yucatán and beyond - their cenotes, cave systems, survey maps and photos, made by and for cave divers.
welcome.invite: Dived somewhere we're missing? Spotted an old depth, a wrong entrance or a map we don't have? Create a free account and help us keep the cave data complete and up to date - every diver's notes count.
welcome.beta: We're in beta. Changes you make aren't permanent yet: all the data can be replaced at any moment. So this is the perfect time to explore the edit tools - go ahead, poke around, you can't break anything for good! Create an account and we'll let you know when the beta is over.
